claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.
A thermally sprayed alumina-based protective coating will enhance the high-temperature oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Thermal spraying or a similar deposition method can form a dense refractory oxide layer on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited alumina or similar refractory oxide layer will act as a physical diffusion barrier.
The deposited layer will prevent oxygen from penetrating the underlying alloy.
The coating will establish a stable, adherent, and dense oxide scale on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The stable, adherent, and dense oxide scale will reduce oxygen ingress.
Reduced oxygen ingress will mitigate further oxidation and pesting.
Mitigating oxidation and pesting will preserve the alloy's microstructure and mechanical integrity.
Relative to untreated material, coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will have a significantly lower oxide-scale thickness after a 5-hour exposure in air at 800–1000 °C.
Relative to untreated material, coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit fewer pesting effects after a 5-hour exposure in air at 800–1000 °C.
The coated material will maintain its tensile ductility and yield strength after the stated oxidation exposure.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes oxidation that leads to pesting and potential degradation.
The proposed intervention is intended for air exposures at 800–1000 °C lasting about 5 hours and for mechanical testing at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
